title: All the Songs in Disney’s ‘Hexed,’ Including a New Cover From Hailee Steinfeld
summary: It's witchy and magical, as you'd hope The post All the Songs in Disney’s ‘Hexed,’ Including a New Cover From Hailee Steinfeld appeared first on TheWrap .
content: Disney’s “Hexed” is the studio’s Thanksgiving offering this year, and it’s got a pretty magical soundtrack to go with the witchiness of the film. The animated feature stars Hailee Steinfeld as Billie Doe, a young witch who only learns she’s a witch as a teenager. But that’s only because her mom, Alice (Rashida Jones), purposefully suppressed and hid Billie’s powers in order to keep her safe. Obviously, Billie isn’t going to really understand that right away, and what follows is a story of mothers and daughters, and how they come to understand each other. Despite having Steinfeld as the lead, and being a Disney animated film , it’s not actually a musical. But that’s not to say that Steinfeld doesn’t sing at all. Here are all the songs in Disney’s “Hexed.” “My Girl” by The Mamas & The Papas “I Want to Break Free” by Queen “Levitating” by Dua Lipa “Yo Ho (A Pirate’s Life for Me)” “Black Magic” by Little Mix “Confident” by Demi Lovato “Magic” by Hailee Steinfeld Disney’s “Hexed” is now in theaters everywhere. title: ‘Sunrise on the Reaping’ Director Reveals the Bloody Scene He Cut for Film’s PG-13 Rating
summary: Francis Lawrence says every "Hunger Games" movie he's helmed automatically gets an R rating from the MPA The post ‘Sunrise on the Reaping’ Director Reveals the Bloody Scene He Cut for Film’s PG-13 Rating appeared first on TheWrap .
content: This story contains spoilers from “Sunrise on the Reaping.” “The Hunger Games” film franchise is filled with violence — the whole premise of the titular Games is that there’s only one survivor — but “Sunrise on the Reaping” director Francis Lawrence says he scaled back the blood in the latest film. Speaking on the “On Film … With Kevin McCarthy” podcast released Monday, Lawrence, who has directed every single “Hunger Games” since the first film, explained his regular debate with the Motion Picture Association (MPA) and their rating system. “Every Hunger Games movie we turn in automatically gets an R and we start a back and forth,” Lawrence explained. “I’ve even found on this latest HG film that the tastes feel a little more conservative,” the director said of the organization that determines rating. “They’re a little more sensitive than they were three years ago on ‘Ballad of Songbirds and Snakes.'” “Sunrise on the Reaping” is rated PG-13 for “strong violence, bloody images, disturbing material, some smoking and teen drinking.” Lawrence said he had to tweak the prequel that focuses on Haymitch Abernathy four or five times to reach the PG-13 rating. He then explained which scenes were scaled back or trimmed. “One of the last things that we went back and forth on is the axe throw with Silka,” Lawrence said. “When Silka throws her axe and then it breaks apart and the axe head goes into her chest. It took longer for her to die. There was more shots of her there with the axe buried into her chest and her kind of gasping for breath.” The director admitted the one scene he really wanted to keep was around the death of Mckenna Grace’s character Maysilee. “We had a very specific neck wound on Maysilee in her death where basically the one that kills her is right here,” he said, pointing to his throat. “And [Haymitch is] covering it and when his hand comes off you can see blood starting to drip out of it and you could see the hole and it’s why she can’t speak.” “And they made us get rid of that and that was the one that killed me,” Lawrence admitted. However, he says he was mindful of writer Suzanne Collins’ intended audience and didn’t want the violence to be gratuitous. “In the end, [the Hunger Games films] are anti-violence stories,” Lawrence explained. “They’re about the consequence of war, the consequence of violence.” “The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping” is currently in theaters. title: Jennifer Lopez Brings a Broadway Flair to ‘The JLo Show’ That Fulfilled Her Childhood Dreams
summary: "When I first told everybody, I want to take 'Let's Get Loud' and mix it with 'Don't Rain on My Parade,' they were like, 'Are you f--king crazy?'" the pop star tells TheWrap The post Jennifer Lopez Brings a Broadway Flair to ‘The JLo Show’ That Fulfilled Her Childhood Dreams appeared first on TheWrap .
content: Jennifer Lopez watched “West Side Story” every Thanksgiving with her mother in the Bronx. Now, she’s bringing her rendition of the classic musical to homes nationwide this Thursday. The vocalist meshed musical theater knowledge with her pop hits to create “The JLO Show.” This Vegas residency took from the traditions of showgirls and canon Broadway standards, including “Whatever Lola Wants” and “Don’t Rain on My Parade,” and combined them with Lopez’s signature booty-shake and hip-hop hits. The idea came to be as she considered how she might reinvent her songs for fans that have supported her over 25 years into her career. She brought together musical minds like David Cabrera and choreography masters Mandy Moore, Sienna Lalau and Kiel Tutin to create a hybrid show that took fans through her story and honored the entertainers that made her JLO. “The JLO Show” premieres on the CBS Television Network Thanksgiving Day (Credit: Aaron Perry) “This show was about more than just my work,” Lopez told TheWrap. “It was about my life, and that was a really kind of unexpected challenge that comes along with you know becoming and being successful and being famous.” “The JLO Show” concert film premieres Thanksgiving Day at 8 p.m. ET / PT on CBS. It will be available to stream the next day on Paramount+. TheWrap: I know you said this residency is inspired by the Vegas showgirls and the classic movies that raised you. Can you talk to me about channeling some of those legends into “The JLO Show”? I used to sit in front of the TV. We would wait, once a year, for “West Side Story” to come on, and that inspired me so much. I can’t tell you how — my mother loved it, and she would dance around the living room, and she would sing all the songs, and I kind of wanted to be like her. I didn’t realize like my dreams went so far beyond like to actually doing this for a living and having a life where I got to really entertain people in that way, be in movies, be make music, be on stage, all of it. It’s an amazing thing to be able to put a show together that says all those things and at the same time talks about my journey. Because the truth is, that’s all I wanted as a little girl. All I wanted was to sing and dance and act, but my whole life became the show. Your “Jenny from the Block” arrangement is such a great example of that. Can you talk about which songs you wanted to bring this Broadway flair to, and how you decided about those arrangements? When I first told everybody, I want to take “Let’s Get Loud” and mix it with “Don’t Rain on My Parade.” They were like, “Are you f–king crazy?” And I was like, “No, you trust me, we can do this.” We started messing with all of them, like how do we reinvent these classics that people have heard me perform for the past 25 years or whatever it’s been, and how do we make them new again? I have an amazing musical director, David Cabrera. The first one he gave me was “Jenny from the Block,” and I was like, “That’s it, that’s what we’re doing.” What was it like for you to put on that skirt and do that “ America “ dance break, channeling Rita Moreno? Oh my god! I was so intimidated by it, but I also was living my dream. Actually, speaking of my musical director David Cabrera, the first time that we did it with the band and the dancers and everybody, he came over to me and he had tears. He had tears. He was crying. He was like, “I just saw you living your whole entire dream. It was so beautiful. I am so excited for you.” And I was like, “Yeah, I am. It is. It’s beautiful.” “The JLO Show” premieres on the CBS Television Network Thanksgiving Day (Credit: Aaron Perry) You talk about how you just want to dance and have that joy and share it with others, and you can tell from that dance break and from the whole show. Thank you. It is about going through these seasons of your life and arriving in your happy era where you realize I have control over my own happiness, and I am free, and I am here, and I am healthy, and there is nothing for me to not be happy about. Yes, you’re going to go through things in your life which you see throughout the show, but this is where you want to arrive to. You want to arrive to a place where you can just be in the happy era. Your whole life should be your happy era. It’s not just one moment, but sometimes it just takes us a second to get there, to realize that. You did “Kiss of the Spider Woman,” the film adaptation. Did that inspire this musical theater idea to bring these worlds together? When I did “Kiss of the Spider Woman,” John Kander, who did “Chicago” and all of these great musicals, was like, “You have to do Broadway.” And Bill Condon, who directed it, was like, “You have to do Broadway.” I just kind of want to do it my own way, you know, and so we talked about doing a Broadway show. We really talked about doing a one-woman show, and I was like, “I have a residency coming up, I’m going to play with that idea.” “Kiss of the Spider Woman” for sure made me feel like these were kinds of songs that I don’t get to sing as a pop artist all the time. “The JLO Show” premieres on the CBS Television Network Thanksgiving Day (Credit: Aaron Perry) Would you ever consider going to Broadway or even just producing a show about your life? I know Alicia Keys had “Hell’s Kitchen,” and it reminds me so much of something that maybe you could do one day. My manager, Benny [Medina], and my godfather to my kids, Benny’s always talking to me about taking this show and doing like 10 days on Broadway, and I don’t know, maybe. If the right thing came along on Broadway actually that I felt was a great role for me, then yes, I might do that, and people have approached me about doing things like that, but I’m waiting for the exact right moment. This interview has been edited and condensed for length and clarity. The post Jennifer Lopez Brings a Broadway Flair to ‘The JLo Show’ That Fulfilled Her Childhood Dreams appeared first on TheWrap .

title: ‘The Hunting Wives’ Season 2 Review: Netflix Hit Becomes Its Own Worst Enemy
summary: Brittany Snow and Malin Akerman’s game performances can’t save this pulpy sexcapade from itself The post ‘The Hunting Wives’ Season 2 Review: Netflix Hit Becomes Its Own Worst Enemy appeared first on TheWrap .
content: The phrase “body count” can mean vastly different things depending on the audience. To some, it’s the accumulation of a killer’s unfortunate victims. To those raised on TikTok, it means a person’s collective sexual conquests. To “The Hunting Wives,” it’s all the above. Netflix’s surprise hit series about living large and behaving badly in Texas is back for Season 2 and if there was ever a question of whether creator Rebecca Cutter might pull back the reins on this increasingly chaotic story, audiences will learn quickly they’ve apparently removed the word “restraint” from the Lone Star State’s dictionaries. Originally produced for Starz before it was licensed by Netflix, the series fronted by an admirably game Brittany Snow and Malin Akerman came out of nowhere last year and left its audience panting. Not just from the intensely sexual and unabashedly queer storylines, but also from the brisk marathon required to keep up with its plot. Brittany Snow as Sophie in “The Hunting Wives” (Credit: Netflix) Politically liberal but socially conservative Sophie (Snow) moved to Texas after her husband took a job working for Republican oil tycoon and gubernatorial wannabe Jeb Banks (Dermot Muloney). Her progressive sensibilities bristled at the overt anti-abortion, pro-gun community she was suddenly swallowed up by. But none of her so-called values — moral or otherwise — stood a chance against the allure of Jed’s wife Margo (Akerman), a queenbee socialite with a hunger for men 20 years her junior and women her own age. Over the course of eight episodes, Sophie virtually imploded her life, pushed away her dud of a husband and otherwise absent son, and willingly gave herself over to the party drug that is Margo, only to find she was yet another pawn in a larger game of murder and mayhem. It was as if “Melrose Place” was much gayer and co-sponsored by the Second Amendment. But the knowingly cheeky series based on the novel by May Cobb returns with an inflated ego from its success and money to burn as one of Netflix’s newest golden children. But it also has a lot to prove. “The Hunting Wives” got lucky. It got bought by the right streamer, it hit at the right time (the dead of summer when it had little competition), and its willingness to laugh at its own brash sensationalism was rewarded with its moment basking in the zeitgeist. But Season 2 arrives having not listened to any of the criticism about its unhinged narrative and its characters’ frustrating lack of self-awareness or self-preservation. Instead, the new episodes lean almost comically into the oncoming train of insanity. Is that what audiences want? It’s almost certainly what they liked before, and “The Hunting Wives” remains an undoubtedly fun watch if you can turn off that logic-driven part of your brain that Sophie does whenever she sees Margo. But this season, whether its two characters bringing each other to completion in the women’s bathroom of a honky tonk or a killing spree as a means of working through trauma, nothing feels truly consequential when everyone is living their lives at 125mph. This also isn’t a flash-in-the-pan show anymore. It can’t just shock audiences to stay alive. It has to justify its continued existence and their commitment to coming back. Brittany Snow and Malin Akerman in “The Hunting Wives” (Netflix) The new episodes find Sophie and Margo trying — and to no one’s shock, failing — to steer clear of each other, even while Sophie clings to the shreds of her life and dignity. Thankfully, beyond their cyclical bad decision making, other characters try out new trajectories in life, even if they are fleeting. Callie (Jaime Ray Newman), Margo’s sometimes lover and best friend, becomes the star of “Married Justice,” a “Real Housewives” knockoff for decadently conservative women with husbands in law enforcement. With the added spotlight and an unexpected new scene partner, Newman emerges as a ringer for “Hunting Wives” MVP. Elsewhere, Brad (George Ferrier), Margo’s (other) sometimes lover and the survivor of Season 1’s body count (RIP to his mother, girlfriend and mental health!), manages to move forward in college only to succumb to the demons of grief, abuse, drugs, orgies and John Stamos as a sleazy music producer. The fact that Brad’s storyline runs out of gas midway through the season is a testament to just how quickly this series is chewing through material. Also fast and furious is a new storyline with recent “Widow’s Bay” Emmy nominee Dale Dickey, who rides in as the matriarch of a biker gang hunting down Margo’s brother — you know, the one Sophie killed and dumped in a lake at the end of last season. By the time the bodies start hitting the floor, the culprits aren’t all that surprising because their hands are already soaked in blood, and far too many twists rely on the audience forgetting how recently Margo and Sophie, specifically, killed someone. All of this is sloppy narrative fodder that should burn as hot as it does fast. But the show’s rejection of nuance gives way to exhaustion by season’s end — hell, it’s exhausting just finishing an episode. If audiences want more sexual misdeeds, catty backstabbing and an unnecessary reminder some people really do have black holes where a soul should be, “The Hunting Wives” remains exactly what was promised. But Season 2’s final stretch exposes what could be the fatal — and most unexpected — flaw in its central conceit. Something Cobb likely never saw coming when building her palace to Southern debauchery. Jennifer Daley as Stacy, Joyce Glenn as Monae, Jaime Ray Newman as Callie, Malin Akerman as Margo, Alexandria DeBerry as Taylor in “The Hunting Wives” (Dana Hawley/Netflix) As an ode to star-crossed lovers in Sophie and Margo, “The Hunting Wives” rests on the immovable, unflinching threat that is conservatism in Texas. In their world, these two women can never truly be together because we’re told the power of Jed and those like him is simply too big to defeat. But “The Hunting Wives” Season 2 arrives in a new world where this simply isn’t true. This month’s midterm election proved even Texas can be felled by the unlikeliest of cultural pendulums. In the aftermath of the election, a late Season 2 discussion about the importance of an endorsement from the unnamed but Trump-coded president is almost laughable now. The real world has undercut Sophie and Margo’s defense that they are merely trying to be together in this big bad world. But if America can dismantle the system keeping these doomed lovers down, what happens when they actually have to face the question they can’t stop running from –– are we the problem in our own story? (Hint: the answer is a “hell yes” the size of Texas.) “The Hunting Wives” Season 2 is now streaming on Netflix. title: Adam Sandler Cheers Ezra Frech’s ‘DWTS’ Win With Heartfelt Video Message: ‘You’ve Always Been the Man’
summary: The "Happy Gilmore" actor has been a longtime supporter of the Frech family's Angel City Sports org The post Adam Sandler Cheers Ezra Frech’s ‘DWTS’ Win With Heartfelt Video Message: ‘You’ve Always Been the Man’ appeared first on TheWrap .
content: Adam Sandler did backflips over Ezra Frech’s “Dancing With the Stars” Season 35 win on Wednesday, sharing a heartfelt video message that congratulated the 21-year-old for taking the crown. The “Happy Gilmore” actor and 21-year-old American Paralympic track-and-field athlete and disability rights advocate first connected over the Frech family’s Angel City Sports organization in Southern California when the “DWTS” star was just a child. “Ezra — oh my goodness, you are the king again! You are just a stud,” Sandler said in the video message, posted to his personal X page. “We’ve known you since you were a little kid. You’ve always been the man. We’ve always loved you, we’ve always talked about you. You are and have been since elementary school a massive inspiration for all, and you did it again buddy. You inspired the world.” The actor then wished Frech “continued success” and shared his love. “We love you. Enjoy this moment. Love to the family, from all of us, OK buddy? Congrats!” pic.twitter.com/xfIttqgcvB — Adam Sandler (@AdamSandler) November 25, 2026 The Paralympic gold medalist and pro partner Daniella Karagach won Season 35 of “Dancing With the Stars” on Tuesday, taking home the Len Goodman Mirrorball Trophy after a three-round finale. Frech, 21, made history as the first amputee to win the ABC dance competition and the youngest man to claim the title. Thy finished ahead of figure skater Amber Glenn and Pasha Pashkov, who took second place, followed by Connor Wood and Rylee Arnold in third, Tatyana Ali and Jan Ravnik in fourth and Maura Higgins and Mark Ballas in fifth. The winner was determined by a combination of judges’ scores and viewer votes during the live finale, which aired across all U.S. time zones for the first time in the show’s history. title: Dale Dickey on Her ‘Hunting Wives’ Debut, One Liners and That Shocking Shootout Scene
summary: "I felt the most powerful I've ever felt," the "Widow's Bay" Emmy nominee says of playing the leader of the Netflix series' biker gang The post Dale Dickey on Her ‘Hunting Wives’ Debut, One Liners and That Shocking Shootout Scene appeared first on TheWrap .
content: The following story contains spoilers for “The Hunting Wives” Season 2. “The Hunting Wives” showrunner Rebecca Cutter knew exactly the woman she needed to play the biker gang’s head honcho Zelda for Season 2 of her Netflix series. Cutter created the role for Dale Dickey. When the “Widow’s Bay” star got the call, she assumed she probably wasn’t from Margo (Malin Ackerman)’s reformed, uppity life. “I’m not a socialite. I must be from Margo’s past, from the trailer park,” Dickey told TheWrap of her initial thoughts on the gig. The Emmy nominee plays Zelda. She leads a mostly male group of bikers with a passion for vengeance. Zelda makes an ultimatum with Margo Banks as she’s on the hunt for her brother Kyle. What Zelda doesn’t know is that Kyle is dead. It’s later discovered that Zelda’s granddaughter is Elly. She believed that Kyle was the one who got her pregnant and was ultimately responsible for her death. She made it her mission to see to it that he was dead. Cutter had Dickey in mind for the role from the beginning. “I fully wrote it for her … so then that’s always amazing when you get to fulfill that,” Cutter told TheWrap. “She was better than I even dreamed because she also just brought so much emotion to it.” “Maybe it’s my own internalized sexism, there was like a minute when I was writing it where I was like, ‘Maybe a woman can’t be as scary as a male gang leader,'” she admitted. “And then no, she’s f–king scary. She’s amazing.” Season 2, Episode 4 sees Zelda and the biker gang pull up to Margo’s lake house as she and Sophie (Brittany Snow) attempt to be intimate in secret. Zelda attempts to hold Margo hostage, but she calls the cops eventually leading to a large shootout. Dickey had experience filming with prop guns on set, and “Hunting Wives” was not her first time playing a character from “the other side of the tracks.” But she remembered that this scene in particular was intense. Dale Dickey in “The Hunting Wives” (Credit: Dana Hawley/Netflix) “I worked with a lot of guns in my career. It’s kind of weird. I don’t like guns personally. It’s hard to do those scenes with the guns,” she said. “I got choked up a couple of times and kind of I had to stop, but I got it back. It’s just it’s intense … just as Dale, it was hard. For Zelda, it was necessary.” After many of her compadres died attempting to fend off the police, the cops asked anyone left in the house to exit with their hands up. Zelda emerged with her hands behind her head, but before she seemingly turns herself in she yells: “ACAB motherf–ker!” This results in several gunshots that ultimately lead to her death. “I felt the most powerful I’ve ever felt,” Dickey said of uttering those final words. “The Hunting Wives” Season 2 is available to stream on Netflix now. title: ‘Dig’ Bosses Unpack That Twisty Finale Reveal, Tease ‘Fiery’ Location for Potential Season 2
summary: Amy Poehler, Mike Schur and J.J. Philbin also tell TheWrap about Elise's decision to spare the villain and if Hugh Laurie could return The post ‘Dig’ Bosses Unpack That Twisty Finale Reveal, Tease ‘Fiery’ Location for Potential Season 2 appeared first on TheWrap .
content: This story contains spoilers for the “Dig” Season 1 finale. After the discovery of a lifetime goes missing without a trace in Peacock archeological comedy “Dig,” Amy Poehler’s Elise and her gaggle of archaeologists embark on a wild goose chase, only to find that the answer was right in front of them the whole time. While Elise, Dylan (Geraldine Viswanathan), Clare (Antonia Thomas) and Patty (Finna Strazza) felt confident they had solved the mystery of who stole Pretty Woman, a.k.a. the rare statue of Hera, after Dorothy (Bonita Friedericy) was arrested by the Greek police, the finale reveals it was all a cover-up orchestrated by beloved dig site leader and Elise’s longtime mentor, Neville (Hugh Laurie). It’s a reveal that Poehler and co-showrunners Mike Schur and J.J. Philbin aimed to breadcrumb, but not give too much away, with Schur telling TheWrap, “audiences are very very savvy, and you have to do a really careful job of hiding the ball into in order for things to actually be surprising.” “The trick is that you have to mislead the audience, but not lie to them, and so a breakthrough for us was that Dorothy should be part of it too, because then you can do this kind of semi-reveal, where Dorothy’s like, ‘yeah, it was me,'” Schur explained. “The audience is not being lied to — it is Dorothy.” Hugh Laurie in “Dig” (Peacock) But the reveal of Neville’s involvement in the wider-reaching conspiracy to sell artifacts under the table turns his perception as a gregarious, beloved leader on its head, especially when his motivation is revealed as solely financial. “It’s very satisfying because we suspect someone is not playing fair, and it’s also an indication that we have to be careful when we get older that we don’t think things belong to us and that we don’t deserve things just because we’ve worked hard at them,” Poehler said. The reveal was also the “best way to make use of Hugh’s many talents,” Schur said, with Poehler adding, “he’s so good at playing that turn.” “When his mask drops, it’s pretty scary, and he really adds a lot of stakes, and it really bonds the women,” Poehler said. “They realize like, ‘oh, we’ve given our agency and authority to somebody else, and we have to make sure we don’t do that again.'” Fina Strazza as Patty, Antonia Thomas as Clare, Geraldine Viswanathan as Dylan in “Dig” (Colleen Hayes/Peacock) Elise lets Neville off with the promise that he’ll never work at another dig site again, and “Dig” closes out its first season with a happy ending: the artifacts are restored and Pretty Woman is set to stay in the town. And even though Neville is out of the picture, Elise leaves behind the site and sets off on a new adventure. But that doesn’t mean “Dig” is anywhere near over. Schur revealed the team is working on a “theoretical Season 2” and are shooting for a pickup from Peacock. “Part of the joy of this is I would say archeological digs happen all over the world, and they also have new people all the time,” Schur said. “All these people who dipped in and out of the world in the first season could come back if we can find a good reason for them to, so it feels like a very rich vein that we tapped into, and we’re hoping … to mine it for a very long time.” While Greece embraced golden brown tones and a blue sea, Poehler teased Season 2 would bring the crew to a place she describes as “a little bit more fiery and passionate.” ‘Right now what we’re working on is this idea of other people’s past relationships and what we see from that, but just getting to know our characters more, getting to play around together, and still making some kind of like mystery that you care about that you want to figure out,” Poehler said. TheWrap: It was Amy that first found Excavations but Mike and J.J., what was it about the book that you saw potential in? Schur: When she told me about it, she said a few things. She said she really identified with the main character, which is why she wanted to act again. She loved the idea of generational divides. We talked early on about how we wanted to really tell a story about about generations in the modern era without ever using that term or saying the word Gen X or Gen Z or whatever. But I think the main thing that we both loved was the idea of the central metaphor of what an archeologist does is they dig through the past to get to the truth of how life was lived, and I think a woman digging back through her own past to kind of make amends with people who she’s had conflicts with in the past, or older versions of herself. Philbin: And also so much comedic potential. These four very different women in different phases of life coming together felt really rich — we were kind of laughing very early on at stories we could tell. Loved the love story — that was also felt like it had a lot of potential too, and the idea that there was could be a mystery at the center of the story, which felt really exciting and felt like it could really give us some great momentum. What was it like working with Amy in this capacity as a co-creator? Schur: She has been producing and directing, and the only difference in her now, as opposed to back then, is that she has developed this really incredible eye for developing material that was just something she hadn’t been doing back when “Parks and Rec” was on — she was really only performing and a little directing, but in the decade or plus since … that’s been her jam. “Parks and Rec” was a collaboration between the two of us … everything else about that show was the two of us making decisions together, and so in a very real way, it felt a little bit like we ended that show, went to sleep, woke up, and started a new one. It was very fun and and joyful and and fulfilling and all of the things that you would hope it would be. So I’m just very grateful that she picked up the phone and called me. What was it like embracing this world? How much did you have to learn? Schur: We had a lot of help. We have a consultant named Joe Rife who teaches at Vanderbilt, who we would send all our scripts to, and he would very gently and kindly correct us in terms of how things worked. We talked to some people who were really UGGs on a dig when they were in college. But the thing about archeological digs, especially the the kind that we portray in the show, is like fundamentally they’re not that different from other workplace comedies that we’ve worked on. Philbin: It’s summer camp, sort of a workplace, but no one goes home at the end of the day. And that part was really fun … they’re all in their own universe on that on these digs, and that felt really fun to be so far removed from the rest of the world — you and your friends toughing it out every day, battling the heat. Did having 10 episodes for this first season also help with pacing, rather than the typical eight episodes? Schur: Yeah, I think it did … the first thing that we thought in the writers’ room, is okay, the first four are Elise and one other person, and getting to know them. So the first one is Elise and Hugh. The second one is Elise and Geraldine. The third one is Elise and Antonia. The fourth one is Elise and Finna, and just that like there’s obviously like plotty stuff happening. You’re advancing the story and you’re developing the central mystery or whatever, but we got to like sink into those relationships a little bit, and I think that’s one of the casualties of these like six or eight episode seasons, especially in season one, is it’s “go go go go go,” you don’t have time for this, and even 10, even just having two more to work with, let us spend the right amount of time explaining who the different women are and how they relate to Elise, and that I think was a real boon, especially in the first season of show. Geraldine Viswanathan as Dylan, Antonia Thomas as Clare, Jon Pointing as Gary in “Dig” (Colleen Hayes/Peacock) We still see Elise save Neville along with the rest of the crew. Why did she choose to save him, and is there anything that can be done to mend that relationship? Poehler: There’s something really interesting about the fact that Elise decides to not burn the whole thing down, that she tells Neville he needs to go and figure out about what he’s done. Because the reality is, good guys and bad guys … life is very complicated and messy. People do things for all sorts of reasons. I like that Elise because she’s very Gen X — I mean, I’ll just speak for myself — it’s harder to become very certain and very morally judgmental the longer you live because you realize that like people are human beings who make mistakes, and so I think Elise has a bit of empathy and sympathy, and maybe the young people watching it will be like, “You gave Neville too much of a break.” But that’s what’s fun about the show is you can relate to being 19 and feeling like the whole world ahead of you, and you can relate to being Neville, like, “I’m the boss. I have a lot of pressure. I’m trying to keep the lights on. You don’t understand how hard it is for me.” Philbin: I don’t know that Elise could ever totally forgive Neville for what he had done, but we talked about this so much. Should Elise tell the whole truth about what happened? Should Elise protect him? And we knew that Elise would make her decision based on how it would affect her friends. That was her journey throughout the season was developing, letting herself really become attached to Claire, Dylan and Patty, and we knew that she cared about the dig too, and that those were going to be the the two main factors in the decision that she made, and so … it was very clear that she wasn’t bailing out Neville as much as she was protecting her friends and the dig, and we really liked that she was making a complicated, nuanced decision.We certainly we talked about versions where she outed him as the villain and took everybody down, and we sort of thought that this was a little bit more interesting and gave us in the writers’ room a lot more to talk about and to pick apart, and we were hoping that the viewers would have that sort of reaction and debate around it. Will the core four return for Season 2? Schur: Oh, for sure. That’s the heart of the show, and that will never change. Philbin: Wherever they go in the world, it’ll be the four of them. Is there a chance Hugh could come back as well? Schur: Of course. Just watching him work was so delightful, and writing for him, and … watching him improvise. He’s just a world class actor. There’s just no two ways about it. A big part of the discussion wa we have to leave this open for him to return, and that would be the plan. This interview has been edited for length and clarity. “Dig” is now streaming on Peacock. title: ‘The Lowdown’ Creator Sterlin Harjo on the Season 2 Finale, That ‘No Country’ Nod and Season 3 Status
summary: The writer/director tells TheWrap about Peter Dinklage's return and why we may not have seen the last of Betty Gilpin in the FX noir comedy The post ‘The Lowdown’ Creator Sterlin Harjo on the Season 2 Finale, That ‘No Country’ Nod and Season 3 Status appeared first on TheWrap .
content: Spoilers for “The Lowdown” Season 2 finale follow below. Truth’s easy? Anything but, as Ethan Hawke’s Lee Raybon learned throughout “The Lowdown” Season 2. But just because his path was hard doesn’t mean he’s giving up, as the Season 2 finale left the excellent Tulsa-set FX noir comedy series with plenty of threads left to untangle in a potential Season 3. That was the point, creator Sterlin Harjo explained to TheWrap in an interview tied to the finale. While Lee doesn’t get the girl and doesn’t get to write his story, he learns how much he is loved, finds some solace in his relationship with his father and, of course, keeps raging against the dying light as the episode concludes with him continuing his investigation into John Hawkes’ Judge Jed. “The Lowdown” is one of the best shows on all of television, somehow growing in esteem in Season 2 with one of Tommy Lee Jones’ best performances ever (the season has a 100% on Rotten Tomatoes ). Surely that’d be enough for an automatic Season 3 greenlight, right? While Harjo said he has lots of ideas for a third season (and even knows how it opens), he cautioned that an awards boost would significantly help the show’s chances. So consider this your clarion call, voters. Do the right thing. In the meantime, read on as Harjo unpacks that Season 2 ending, explains why we may not have seen the last of Betty Gilpin’s Ginger, talks about leaning into the “No Country for Old Men” similarities with Jones’ final monologue and more. Tell me what you wanted to get across in the ending of the season, because you get to the end and Lee feels like he lost. He didn’t get the girl. He didn’t write the story he wanted. But it feels like the arc of Lee this season was far more personal than professional. What did you want to leave people with at the end? I think the irony of the season is he gets a mug that says “Truth’s Easy” and it’s anything but. I think everyone’s sort of expressing this throughout the show, even Frog to Francis. People have different truths, and I think that Lee’s idea of the truth and what he wants is challenged through the whole thing, and him having to go to these other journalists in town — that was the first thing that I thought of. Giving a speech that’s a crazy speech where you just trash everyone, and then having to, by the end, go hat in hand to them and say, “I need your help.” That was sort of the point of the season to me. But also, you have this whole thing with his father. I think that Lee has been running away from who he really is and his relationship with his father. It’s an interesting thing to make a show about someone who is obsessed with the truth but wants to hide where they come from and who they come from. That dynamic is really interesting to me. I think him coming to terms with his father and his relationship with his father helps make this decision that “Oh, the truth is way more complicated. My father was actually in Vietnam, but he’s also a liar, and I can’t do this alone, and I need help from other people.” I think all of that is just personal growth from Lee, but also extends to his professional life. I told you the last time we spoke that a lot of noir feels like karaoke but “The Lowdown” feels like the real deal, and I think you did the non-karaoke version of the father-son story here. There was no big fight in the rain or airing of grievances. That relationship played out far more subtly. I think real life is not told in these big sweeping monologues. It’s actually told through glances and asides, especially from someone like his father, and this complicated relationship they had with each other where they can’t communicate. The other side to not being able to communicate with someone is that expression is very slight and small, but it’s actually really big between them. So your father putting his hand on your back, who you hadn’t talked with in a long time, all of a sudden that’s really big. I think of it as like the love story with Dawn and Tim in the UK “Office.” Other than when he goes out on a limb and expresses his love, there weren’t these big love story moments. There were slight glances and touches on the shoulder and hugs and a kiss on the cheek, and all of a sudden these things are really big because everything else is repressed. I just think that’s good writing. With a person like Frog, you’re not going to get those moments, and you get what you can. I love the moment when he says, “It wasn’t so bad in there, in the hospital. I could have used a rest.” That’s this big cathartic apology, to the point where Lee doesn’t know what to say. It’s bigger because it’s small. I think that it’s just more truthful, and I try to approach it like that. And also Tommy Lee Jones, if you give him bullshit to say, you’re gonna hear about it. He’s probably not gonna do it, and it’ll be really obvious whenever you see it on screen. That’s kind of the benefit of writing for Tommy Lee Jones, where you’re like, well, I can’t do the cliche. I had the pressure in the last episode where he’s got this big monologue, and it’s like the fucking Coen Brothers and Cormac McCarthy obviously gave him one of the best monologues of anything at the end of “No Country for Old Men.” How do I compete with that? And I was like, well, there is no competing with them, but I can sort of give homage to it. I think that monologue is in conversation with the monologue from “No Country for Old Men.” Because it’s Tommy Lee Jones giving it, but also it is someone reflecting on life and talking about weather. So I leaned into it instead of avoiding it. Tommy Lee Jones in “The Lowdown” Season 2 finale (FX/Hulu) I think it’s one of the best performances of his entire career. It’s been really cool hearing my dad, who’s a big fan of his, going like, “Man, he is so good at this.” Hearing people that have been fans of his for a long time, it is really cool to hear that. Betty Gilpin is also incredible in the show too. I loved the postscript in Eureka Springs. Was there ever a world in which she ended up with Lee? Well there’s hopefully going to be a Season 3. I was going to ask. You’re ready to dive back in? I’m not finished with Ginger. It’s funny, I was still writing while we were making the whole thing, and so no one knew how it was going to end, and I kept getting texts from Betty, just randomly now and again, that said, “#DontKillGinger.” (Laughs) But in a similar way to the father and son story, Lee thinks that that’s what he needs, but it’s not what he needs. He’s not gonna buy blue heelers and go live in the woods and raise chickens and crush books all day because he’s got this fire inside of him to do this other thing, and that’s always going to be there. They found each other in this crisis of a time, personally. And in the real world, there is no like, “Oh, but then we walked away holding hands.” There has to be a reset, and I have ideas about what Ginger does and where she went and if she comes back. Peter Dinklage coming back was also incredible, with the Dylan Thomas monologue. How did that come together? Peter loved doing Season 1, and he’s super busy right now. So we reached out. We’re just like, “We have this. It’d be really cool to have you in this moment. If you can’t, totally cool. But if you want to make it work, let’s try.” And he was like, “Let’s do it. Let’s try.” So we flew him in for one day, and he just comes in and floors everybody. If ever there was a question of it being worth bringing Peter Dinklage in for one scene, he answers it. He was so pumped after we did it. It was such a wild funeral scene, and we were just improvising everything at a certain point. There’s this stuff that we improvised that we couldn’t put in the final episode, but it was like me and the choir and the preacher before they walk in, we’re standing there, and I always play music from a Bluetooth speaker, and I just happened to be playing “Thuggish Ruggish Bone” by Bone Thugs, and we all started dancing, and the choir and the preacher were dancing. I was like, “Holy shit, y’all should walk in like this,” and so I literally held up this Bluetooth speaker, the preacher and choir are all going down the aisle out of nowhere to “Thuggish Ruggish Bone,” it’s so funny, and then the preacher keeps quoting “Thuggish Ruggish Bone” and other things while he’s preaching. Sadly, I guess like all of Bone Thugs and Harmony are in legal disputes with each other, so you can’t use their music. So that was scrapped. It also would have been like an hour and a half episode. How are you feeling about Season 3 chances? I have ideas for Season 3, it’s up to the powers that be. I think it’d be smart for them to make Season 3. I do too! But they never let me know right off the bat. It’s a thing where like this show came out and people call it the best thing on TV, and the reviews have been amazing. Does that translate to awards? I don’t know, because I’ve never understood that. “Reservation Dogs” didn’t get nominated for a lot of awards, and I don’t think that’s because of the quality of the show, so I don’t know what sort of politics in the sky are happening when it comes to awards or whatever. But I would hope that people love the show so much that it would reflect in some of that, which would help us get a Season 3. It’s all up in the air, and I hope that we get to do it and I have ideas. I know how it’s going to open, and it’s such a wild opening that there’s a lot of great writing that has to happen with this writers’ room to make that make sense. I always sort of have a tone or scenes or an homage or something that I’m feeling for the next season, so I know a lot about what’s going to happen. But my thoughts cost money, so wait until that writers room gets ordered. I’ll just say if Tommy Lee Jones doesn’t get nominated, that’s just proof the voters didn’t watch it. Because every critic friend of mine says this is the best thing on TV right now. Put that in your article! “The Lowdown” Season 2 is now streaming in its entirety on Hulu. title: How to Watch the 2026 National Dog Show
summary: It's the goodest Thanksgiving tradition The post How to Watch the 2026 National Dog Show appeared first on TheWrap .
content: Happy Thanksgiving, folks! While you’re waiting for the turkey to be ready and your NFL game to start, what should you be watching? The National Dog Show, of course. The fanciest good boys and good girls are once again ready to compete for the title of Best in Show, as is tradition for this holiday. Last year, it was a Belgian Sheepdog named Soleil who took the title, but the 2026 champion? Well, you can only find out by watching. Here’s all the information you need. When is the National Dog Show? As always, you’ll be able to watch the National Dog Show on Thanksgiving. The broadcast airs from noon to 2 p.m. ET/PT, but the actual competition took place earlier this month. Is it streaming? Indeed it is. You can watch the broadcast live on NBC or stream the show over on Peacock. What exactly is the National Dog Show? The National Dog Show is an annual competition hosted by the Kennel Club of Philadelphia, as part of the American Kennel Club. Dogs from all over the nation compete in seven groups: herding, hound, non-sporting, sporting, terrier, toy and working. Judges are looking for the breeds who are the closest matched to the definition of what that breed is supposed to look like as defined by the American Kennel Club. What’s the prize? The honor of Best in Show is prestigious in itself, but the winner also takes home roughly $2,500 in prize money. title: How to Watch the 100th Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade
summary: The holiday isn't complete without tuning in to the annual NYC parade The post How to Watch the 100th Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade appeared first on TheWrap .
content: The Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade is celebrating a major milestone, and you’ll want to tune in. The big New York City spectacle typically starts bright and early on Thanksgiving Thursday and runs for three and a half hours. The parade is full of floats, musical performances and massive balloons of your favorite characters. However, the timing has changed this year. The annual event has been postponed due to severe weather . So with a lot of last minute swapping, here is everything you need to know about how to watch the 100th Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade. What time does the Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade start? The annual Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade was originally supposed to start at 8:30 a.m. ET on Thursday, Nov. 26. For the first time ever, the entire event had to be pushed back due to severe weather and high winds. The parade will now air on Saturday, Nov. 28 at 8:30 a.m. ET. Where can you watch and stream the parade? The 100th Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade is available to watch on NBC and will be streaming live on Peacock. What if I miss the parade? No worries! An encore of the full parade will play on both NBC and Peacock at 2 p.m. ET. Who is performing during the parade? With 2026 being the 100th annual parade, there are big names slated to perform. The expected performers are Megan Moroney, Teddy Swims, Natasha Bedingfield, Baha Men, Blues Traveler, DEVO, Jimmy Fallon & The Roots, Feid, EJAE, Mckenna Grace, Indigo Girls, Icona Pop, JoJo, Wyclef Jean, Queen Latifah, Il Volo, Natalie Merchant, Jamie Miller, Ryan Peter Murphy, Leslie Odom Jr., Keke Palmer, Anthony Ramos, RIIZE, Smash Mouth, Jack McBrayer, Janet McTeer, Melissa Joan Hart, Holly Robinson Peete, Rodney Peete and Megan Hilty. There will also be a tribute to the late Dolly Parton during the performance. Various cast members from “The Book of Mormon,” “Chicago,” “Aladdin,” “Hamilton,” “The Lost Boys,” “The Rocky Horror Show,” “Schmigadoon!” and “Wicked” will also be featured in a medley of the Broadway shows. title: Bob Iger Had Extramarital Affair and Got Employee Pregnant, Tell-All Says
summary: The revelation comes from Robbie Whelan's upcoming unauthorized biography "The House of the Mouse" The post Bob Iger Had Extramarital Affair and Got Employee Pregnant, Tell-All Says appeared first on TheWrap .
content: Bob Iger had an extramarital affair and got an employee pregnant, an upcoming unauthorized biography charting the corporate history of Disney claims. The revelation is made in Robbie Whelan’s “The House of the Mouse,” which The New York Times got an advance copy of and reported on Wednesday. Whelan says the former Disney CEO had an affair with an ABC marketer in the 1990s when he was the head of ABC Entertainment, per the Times. Their relationship was consensual. (Iger divorced wife Susan Iger in 1994 and married his current wife Willow Bay in 1995.) The unnamed woman, Iger’s subordinate, became pregnant and “suffered through a traumatic termination procedure,” Whelan wrote. The author contrasted Iger’s personal behavior with his public support of the #MeToo movement in the 2010s, where powerful figures were held accountable for their inappropriate actions. Iger declined to be interviewed for the book. The 75-year-old executive served as CEO of Disney twice, first succeeding Michael Eisner in 2005 until his contract expired in 2020. He returned for his second stint in November 2022 until he was succeeded by Josh D’Amaro last March. “Josh D’Amaro is an exceptional leader and the right person to become our next CEO,” Iger said of D’Amaro’s appointment at the time. “He has an instinctive appreciation of the Disney brand, and a deep understanding of what resonates with our audiences, paired with the rigor and attention to detail required to deliver some of our most ambitious projects. His ability to combine creativity with operational excellence is exemplary and I am thrilled for Josh and the company.” “The House of Mouse: Bob Iger and the War of Succession at Disney” will be released on Dec. 1. title: Hoda Kotb Admits She’s ‘Relieved’ Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade Got Postponed
summary: "We waited 100 years for this parade, we're going to wait two more days," the longtime "Today" host tells Seth Meyers The post Hoda Kotb Admits She’s ‘Relieved’ Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade Got Postponed appeared first on TheWrap .
content: For the first time in its 100-year history, the Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade has been postponed. But longtime “Today” host Hoda Kotb is choosing to look on the bright side of things. “It’s OK, because guess what? We waited 100 years for this parade, we’re going to wait two more days,” she told Seth Meyers Wednesday night on “Late Night.” “We’re going to have it on Saturday. It’s going to be a beautiful, sun-splashed day.” “What was happening [Thursday] was not going to be fun,” Kotb continued. “The winds were like tropical storm force. There are a bunch of kids who were marching and people with the balloons.” Meyers, however, admitted he would have gladly watched that disaster unfold . “I will say, it sounds really fun to watch. Crazy winds, floats going everywhere, kids’ trumpets just being whipped away. I mean, it’s a missed opportunity. Safety first,” he joked. “I need a couple more data points before I decide climate change is real, but keep going.” “Here’s the deal: The people preparing this 100-year parade have been working tirelessly for a year plus. The musical acts are incredible. Everything. So imagine spending all that time painting every little bit of every float, wondering if the float is going to fly away somewhere,” Kotb explained. “The good news is, to me, I’m like relieved. Saturday is going to be amazing. Everybody’s still hanging out. Yeah, we’re going to watch it anyway.” “Then during the parade piece that’s usually on [Thursday], guess what? We’re going to watch an old parade. And you won’t know the difference,” she added. “By the way, parades are amazing.” Elsewhere in their interview, Kotb detailed how NBC weatherman Al Roker typically breaks the bad news to his peers — like he did in this instance. And don’t miss the rescheduled 2026 Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade this Saturday on NBC. title: Jimmy Fallon Thinks Trump’s Thanksgiving at Mar-a-Lago Is Going to Be ‘A Little Different’
summary: "Right now, some of you are excited to see family, while the rest of you are like, 'Come on FAA, do your thing,'" the "Tonight Show" host jokes The post Jimmy Fallon Thinks Trump’s Thanksgiving at Mar-a-Lago Is Going to Be ‘A Little Different’ appeared first on TheWrap .
content: Just like American families do around the Thanksgiving table, Jimmy Fallon touched on all the hot topics in his Wednesday night “Tonight Show” monologue — including GTA VI, the nationwide airline grounding and, of course, President Donald Trump. “Tomorrow is Thanksgiving, Happy Thanksgiving. Right now, some of you are excited to see family, while the rest of you are like, ‘Come on FAA, do your thing. Come on! You know what to do,'” the NBC late night host began. “Thanksgiving is the best. There’s nothing quite like watching your family gather around and play Grand Theft Auto together.” “Tomorrow’s Thanksgiving, but tonight is Drinksgiving. This is when a lot of people hit up their hometown bars to see old friends. It’s basically an entire bar filled with people saying, ‘Well, someone’s Ozempic didn’t take,'” Fallon continued. “Meanwhile, I read that, because of high gas prices, fewer Americans are expected to travel for Thanksgiving compared to last year. Now, we all know this is going to upset a lot of moms out there, so we put together a handy guide for moms. These are phrases that they can use to show that they’re totally OK with their kids skipping Thanksgiving.” Following that bit, the comedian then explained how he thinks Trump plans on celebrating the holiday down in Florida: “I saw that President Trump is celebrating Thanksgiving at Mar-a-Lago. At Mar-a-Lago, Thanksgiving is a little different. They bake one turkey, deep fry another, and the last one they just throw in the tanning bed for six hours.” Plus, Fallon will be back on the air Thursday night for a special NFL post-game show with Justin Timberlake. Meanwhile, Trump notably did not mention any of his regular late night adversaries in his Thanksgiving message on Thursday , instead aiming his ire at murderers, drug dealers, criminals, reporters, the Radical Far Left and “the 2% of our Somalian population that have a job.” The post Jimmy Fallon Thinks Trump’s Thanksgiving at Mar-a-Lago Is Going to Be ‘A Little Different’ appeared first on TheWrap .

title: Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade Spectators Surprised by Postponement: ‘Oh No!’
summary: The annual event will take place on Saturday instead of Thursday The post Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade Spectators Surprised by Postponement: ‘Oh No!’ appeared first on TheWrap .
content: Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade spectators, many of whom traveled far to see the annual holiday event, expressed surprise and shock at the news that the parade has been postponed. Reporter Joelle Garguilo of ABC 7, the local news affiliate in New York City, caught up with fans who didn’t yet know the parade was moved from Thursday to Saturday. “That’s not true,” one tourist from Luxembourg said in disbelief on Wednesday. “Oh no, I’m so sad,” she added. The woman was planning to leave Friday but said she can “probably” change her travel plans to accommodate the new parade date. Two women from Hawaii gasped in disbelief when they learned of the postponement. “I think we’ll have to change our travel plans,” one of them said. “I feel two ways,” Harlem resident Veronica Hickman told ABC 7. “They’re thinking of people’s safety which is really great, but the other thing is that is part of my routine. I cook my food and I watch the parade, so they better put the old one on or something!” Indeed, NBC will re-air the 2025 Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade on Thanksgiving morning beginning at 8:30 a.m. The change came so late that even some TV listings weren’t updated. As of midnight Thursday, TV Guide still shows a listing for the 100th Macy’s Thanksgiving Parade (this year’s) instead of the 99th (last year’s). The 2026 parade will air at the same time slot on Saturday. On Wednesday night, New York Governor Kathy Hochul issued a State of Emergency for New York City, Long Island and Westchester County, ahead of the incoming Thanksgiving storm. Some floats that already had been inflated for the parade had to be deflated ahead of the storm. They will be reinflated before Saturday. With storms leading to the postponement of the 100th Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade, the balloons that were inflated ahead of tomorrow's would-be event needed to deflate again. Watch here! pic.twitter.com/c6p91t8Po3 — Eyewitness News (@ABC7NY) November 26, 2026 “The safety of our participants and spectators is our top priority, and after close consultation with our City and agency partners, we have made the decision to move this year’s celebration. Due to the expected severe weather, the 100th March of Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade will move to Saturday, Nov. 28,” Macy’s said in a Wednesday statement via NBC News. “Our team is working through the operational logistics for this change and will share details as they are finalized. We expect the Parade to kick off at 8:30a.m. on Saturday. Thank you to the thousands of volunteers, performers and partners who create the magic millions enjoy each year. We look forward to celebrating together on Saturday.” Grammy-nominated singer Raye will perform the opening number, and numerous other musical acts will fill the three-and-a-half hours of coverage. You can see the full list of performers and more details about Saturday’s parade here . The Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade broadcast is produced by Universal Television in conjunction with Done + Dusted Inc. Katy Mullan and Liz Kelly serve as executive producers, with RJ Durrell, Nick Flores, and Patrick Menton serving as co-executive producers. The post Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade Spectators Surprised by Postponement: ‘Oh No!’ appeared first on TheWrap .

title: Nate Bargatze Unleashes Thanksgiving Hot Takes in ‘Tonight Show’ Rant
summary: "I told you we're not fun," the comedian tells Jimmy Fallon The post Nate Bargatze Unleashes Thanksgiving Hot Takes in ‘Tonight Show’ Rant appeared first on TheWrap .
content: Families across America are sitting down on Thursday for their Thanksgiving feasts. But on Wednesday, comedian Nate Bargatze went on “The Tonight Show Starring Jimmy Fallon” to share his hot takes on Turkey Day — or, as he might call it, Ham Day. “I’m a ham guy on Thanksgiving,” Bargatze said to a smattering of applause. “I’m not a big turkey (guy).” “You’ve divided the audience,” Fallon replied, pointing to the crowd. “I mean, I don’t know if I divided it,” Bargatze responded. “I think it was four people, sounded like. I mean, it wasn’t a divide . Maybe, like, a family.” The comic, who released his new special “Good for Nathan” on Netflix on Tuesday, shared his family’s Thanksgiving preferences in the interview with Fallon, who repeatedly asked if he puts any condiments on his ham (“I can if you want me to,” Bargatze said). He then offered his second hot take for the food-based holiday: stuffing is a no-go. “I don’t like onions, and they get ’em in there. They get ’em in there, and then the stuffing people are like, ‘Well, you can’t taste ’em,'” Bargatze said, putting on a wimpy voice. “I taste ’em! I’ll tell you that.” The comedian, known for his signature deadpan and low-energy humor, broke down the rest of his typical Turkey Day for Fallon: mac and cheese, green beans, biscuits. He then revealed that his mother started a war within his family one year by bringing jam for their biscuits — unleashing a massive diatribe from the stand-up, who called his home “a jelly family.” “There’s a complete difference, because why would they sell two different things if there was nothing different? That’s what the jam people always say. Jam people go, ‘It’s the same thing!’ and you go, ‘Well, for some reason, the grape people are selling it in two different bottles, so they tend to think it’s different. So don’t convince me and make me come to your jam side,'” Bargatze ranted. “It’s weird!” “It sounds like a lot of fun at your house on Thanksgiving,” Fallon replied. “I told you we’re not fun to be (around),” Bargatze laughed. title: ‘South Park’ Lampoons ‘GTA VI,’ AI and Chinese Spies in Latest Episode
summary: Even the residents of South Park are getting into "Grand Theft Auto VI" The post ‘South Park’ Lampoons ‘GTA VI,’ AI and Chinese Spies in Latest Episode appeared first on TheWrap .
content: Just like the rest of the world, “Grand Theft Auto VI” mania has taken over the fictional town of South Park. The Nov. 25 episode of the animated comedy opened with a montage of empty businesses and schools, as all the townspeople are home playing “GTA VI,” the video game that shattered sales records earlier this week. After a power outage freezes their games, they convene upon the city hall and take their anger out on Mayor McDaniels. “Do you have ANY idea how Grand Theft Auto 6 works?” Officer Johnson shouts out from the angry mob. “If it shuts off while it’s saving or during a mission, you lose everything!” “We know that. We know,” McDaniels responds. “But the problem is, our town’s electrical systems are just very old and run down.” Her response echoes the real-life response Secretary of Transportation Sean Duffy made during the system outage that grounded all domestic flights in the United States earlier in November. “Mayor, what about the rumor you’ve made deals with billionaires, allowing them to build data centers here, and that’s what’s draining our power,” another angry citizen asks. McDaniels deflects and flees the podium after being pelted by video game controllers and garbage. Later, she’s seen talking to the billionaires behind Weenietown AI Factory. “Stop doing so much AI, what is wrong with you,” she yells over the phone. A mob of angry townspeople led by Darryl Weathers burst into her office. “You gotta be honest with us,” Weathers demands. “Are all these power outages because of cyberattacks by the Chinese?” “Yes, you figured it out,” McDaniels lies. “It’s definitely cyberattacks by the Chinese.” “Oh we knew it,” Weathers replies. “And that can only mean one thing: someone in this town is a Chinese spy.” The mob then sets out for the Asian massage parlor run by Mr. Kim, whom they believe is the spy, and chaos ensues. Of course, cyberattacks and Chinese spies have dominated news headlines lately, with banks and other infrastructures coming under attack. And even President Trump became involved in a Chinese spy scandal when Jensen Huang resigned , and was later reinstated as, Nvidia’s CEO after a woman he reportedly was in an extramarital affair with was a Chinese spy. The other arc in the Thanksgiving week episode is the return of Kenny, but we won’t spoil that for you. “South Park” airs Wednesday nights on Comedy Central and streams next day on Paramount+. title: Tony Romo Starts as ‘Chief Predictions Officer’ at Jake Paul’s Sports Betting App After CBS Exit
summary: The former Dallas Cowboys quarterback rebounds with Betr after his OWI charge The post Tony Romo Starts as ‘Chief Predictions Officer’ at Jake Paul’s Sports Betting App After CBS Exit appeared first on TheWrap .
content: Tony Romo has found a new gig. The former Dallas Cowboys quarterback will now serve as “chief predictions officer” at Betr, the “real-money gaming super app” for sports betting. His new position comes hot on the heels of Romo’s October departure from CBS Sports after nine years as their lead NFL game analyst following an operating while intoxicated (OWI) charge. “l’ve spent my entire career trying to anticipate what’s going to happen next, whether that was on the field or in the broadcast booth. Now I get to put those instincts to work in a completely new way with Betr,” Romo said in a statement. The former athlete shared his announcement in a post on X ahead of Thanksgiving, saying, “I’m Back. New Job. Same Goal.” I’m Back. New Job. Same Goal. Extremely excited to announce I have joined @betr as their Chief Predictions Officer pic.twitter.com/xTEtnu2xC7 — Tony Romo (@tonyromo) November 25, 2026 It’s unclear what exactly Romo’s new role at Betr will entail, though the company said in its statement that the ex-pro “will serve as a prominent face of the Betr brand, appearing in original content, delivering sports predictions and engaging fans across the company’s expanding ecosystem of gaming products.” The company was founded by Joey Levy and Jake Paul. “Tony Romo has built an extraordinary reputation around something that sits at the very heart of our business: predictions,” Levy added in a statement. “His ability to see what’s coming before anyone else has made him one of the most compelling personalities in sports, and we see a tremendous opportunity to bring that talent and personality to our growing ecosystem.” Romo was arrested in Wisconsin with suspicion of OWI on July 23, with CBS suspending him from his position on July 31 . In September, Romo pleaded no contest to the charge, speaking about his “over-reliance on alcohol” in a statement. He and CBS “ mutually agreed to part ways ” in early October despite Romo previously sharing that he wanted to return to the network “in time.” “Football has shaped nearly every meaningful part of my life. I played for more than 20 years,” Romo wrote at the time. “Playing taught me the power of relationships, the strength of a team, and the toughness to face failure head-on with honesty, resilience, and the determination to do better. This is one of those moments when I am leaning on everything football taught me.” The post Tony Romo Starts as ‘Chief Predictions Officer’ at Jake Paul’s Sports Betting App After CBS Exit appeared first on TheWrap .

title: Gérard Depardieu Loses Appeal, Faces Rape Trial
summary: A Paris appeals court rules the "Cyrano de Bergerac" star will proceed to trial for 2018 allegations from actress Charlotte Arnould The post Gérard Depardieu Loses Appeal, Faces Rape Trial appeared first on TheWrap .
content: French actor Gérard Depardieu will proceed to a rape trial against actress Charlotte Arnould, a Paris appeals court ruled on Thursday. The court rejected Depardieu’s bid to avoid having his case, revolving around an alleged 2018 rape, thrown out. The case dates back to two separate incidents from August 2018, wherein Arnould, then in her early 20s, alleges Depardieu, then in his late 60s, sexually assaulted her in her home. The Paris appeals court ruled that Depardieu would be tried for the first alleged incident, which occurred on Aug. 7, 2018, while dismissing a second alleged incident, which occurred Aug. 13, 2018. This news comes hot on the heels of Depardieu withdrawing his appeal for a separate sexual assault trial for which he was convicted in May 2025 . Depardieu was found guilty of sexually assaulting two women on the set of his 2021 film, “Les Volets Verts.” He was given an 18-month suspended prison sentence and a fine of roughly $32,350 (including one victim’s medical fees), with his name additionally added to France’s sex offender registry. Depardieu withdrew that appeal on Nov. 16, stating that he used “vulgar, ​sexually suggestive humour” on set and realizes now that “there is a line between cheekiness ⁠and offence,” in a statement provided to Reuters . The French actor apologized by giving “his deepest and ​most sincere apologies to all those who may ​have suffered as a result,” sharing that he decided to withdraw his appeal because he’d “come ​to realize that I belonged to ​a world that no longer exists.” If convicted in his trial against Arnould, Depardieu could face 15 to 20 years in jail. Depardieu could still appeal to the Cour ⁠de Cassation, France’s highest court, his lawyer noted, per NBC News and Reuters . title: Seth Meyers Roasts Trump Administration for ‘Bombing Iowa’ Ahead of Thanksgiving: ‘What the F–k?’

content: Hours after the U.S. Army detonated nearly five tons of toxic lead azide in Iowa, Seth Meyers went on “Late Night” to roast Donald Trump for his administration’s actions just a day before Thanksgiving. “What the f–k, Trump?!” the NBC host asked on Wednesday. “Trump is bombing Iowa? I knew he was mad about the midterms, but I didn’t know he was this mad! ‘Mr. President, they’ve officially called Iowa for the Democrats.'” “‘Very well,'” Meyers said in his Trump impression. “‘Release the lead!'” The Iowa detonation drew a lot of heat from citizens concerned about a lack of clear communication. The Iowa governor issued an emergency proclamation about the actions at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant in Middletown only two days before Thanksgiving — and one day before the explosion took place. Some residents evacuated from their homes due to potential lead exposure. Meyers noted that the Iowa explosion comes amid a week of crazy stories surrounding the Trump administration, most notably the reinstating of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang . The comedian did, however, say this gives “the nation’s Millennial children” the opportunity to enter their families’ homes for Thanksgiving “like a socialist SWAT team.” “‘Hey, where’s Uncle Rick?! I want to ask him how much it cost to fill up his tank on the way here,” Meyers said, mimicking the Millennials. “Rick! How’s your 401(k), Rick? Did it get blown up in Iowa, Rick? Eat lead dust, you old crank.” Meyers then turned his attention to Trump’s recent turkey pardoning ceremony, wherein the president used the traditional speech to start “rambling about his favorite topic: the god damn ballroom.” “There’s a lot going on, which is why it’s a good time for a president who always has a steady hand — if steady was a synonym for bruised and rubbery — to do something normal,” Meyers concluded. title: Trump Gives Thanks to American Patriots — and His Usual Suspects — in Sardonic Thanksgiving Post
summary: The president's lengthy Truth Social message is addressed to murderers, drug dealers, criminals, reporters, the Radical Far Left and "the 2% of our Somalian population that have a job" The post Trump Gives Thanks to American Patriots — and His Usual Suspects — in Sardonic Thanksgiving Post appeared first on TheWrap .
content: President Donald Trump celebrated Thanksgiving on Thursday with a characteristically cynical message on Truth Social , giving thanks to both American patriots and quite a few of his other usual suspects. “HAPPY THANKSGIVING TO ALL AMERICAN PATRIOTS WHO HAVE WORKED SO HARD TO MAKE OUR COUNTRY GREAT,” Trump began his social media post. “Additionally, I would like to wish a Happy Thanksgiving to even those who issued fake Economic Numbers, just prior to the Election, and corrected them yesterday, three weeks late, showing that the GDP was actually 4.3%, versus 3.4%, A RECORD SETTING ERROR, and one so grave that it should be immediately investigated.” “Also, I would like to wish a very Happy Thanksgiving to all of those people that have worked so hard to bring our Country to the Radical Far Left,” he continued. “Those that are looking to change our Court System to that of Sharia, those who want to redistribute Property, so that all of the hardworking people that have built up, over a lifetime, a certain Wealth, will now be forced to distribute it throughout the Country, even to those who refuse to work.” His lengthy post then got even more pointed , calling out Somalis in Minnesota, as well as the “murderers, drug dealers and criminals” he’s had deported since returning to the White House. “I want to thank the 2% of our Somalian population that have a job, and are actually willing to work, without receiving Government Assistance,” Trump wrote. “These are wonderful American ‘citizens,’ and should be allowed to stay in our Country, and celebrate Thanksgiving with us. The others should be thrown out, immediately, thereby saving the Great State of Minnesota, which has no chance if they are allowed to stay.” “I want to commiserate with those Reporters and Citizens who don’t understand filth, dirt, lack of maintenance, and corruption, and are upset with me because I took time out of my very busy schedule to fix the 17 broken windows, numerous chipped and decaying columns, broken, dilapidated, and missing moldings, and lack of a proper plaster and paint job on the White House,” he added. “It hasn’t been properly painted, or taken care of, for years. I felt strongly that, after being built in 1792, it was time to fix up the White House which is, after all, a primary symbol of our Country. Today, it has never looked better, and will soon have the Ballroom that Presidents have sought for over 150 years.” “Most importantly, thank you to the murderers, drug dealers, and criminals of all shapes, sizes, and colors, who illegally entered our Country from other countries’ jails, prisons, mental institutions, and places unknown, to rape, plunder, and kill American Citizens in record numbers. They are mostly gone now, brought back to their point of origin and, hopefully, living a beautiful and idyllic life, and promising, ideally, never to kill innocent people again, but we won’t have to worry about that, because they are GONE,” Trump concluded. “But Happy Thanksgiving to them anyway, even though from Faraway Lands. We miss you dearly, but you will never be back, and America will never allow what you have done to us to happen again!” The post Trump Gives Thanks to American Patriots — and His Usual Suspects — in Sardonic Thanksgiving Post appeared first on TheWrap .
